transcript: Okay, the hype is real: Sunset Boulevard is amazing. When Paul and I attended a preview this past weekend, we were not familiar with the story or the score, but we'd heard that Nicole Scherzinger's performance was show stopping, which it absolutely is. She's raw and vulnerable, very funny at times, and her vocals are stellar. Her tone has this smoky quality to it that works so perfectly for this score and this production, and her stage presence is very alluring, like you cannot take your eyes off of her. And when she's not on stage, there's still so much to feast your eyes and ears upon. The direction by Jamie Lloyd is at times jaw-dropping. The use of projections and live camera work is not just creative and visually cool, but really supportive of the story and this particular take on the story. The blend of theater and film gives this production a starkly cinematic and almost voyeuristic quality. Jamie Lloyd is somewhat known for minimalism, but I thought this production was anything but minimal, despite the mostly bare stage. The blocking is striking and with the lighting design and projections, it's rather big production. And the entire cast is great — obviously Nicole, but also Tom Francis as Joe has a lot of stage time and completely captivates with his potent energy and fantastic vocals. I suppose if I had to critique this piece, I'd say at some points the plot gets a tad muddy with everything going on, but the story is simple enough and the big plot points come through just fine. If you already know the story, this isn't really a concern at all. Simply put, this is an unforgettable, must-see production and could easily be THE theatrical event of the season. I'm afraid to overhype and I don't know if this will have universal appeal, but I thought it was really something special. With that, another playbill for my collection.
